focus: P2 authority-plane mapping and adversarial audit of disposable projection, single authority, reducer-version checkpoint invalidation, point-in-time semantics, and audit-preserving compaction
noveltyJustification: Iteration 002 established exact replay, checkpoints, and non-compaction; this adversarial pass adds the current-vs-target authority distinction, maps domain and audit streams as complementary rather than dual authority, identifies same-version reducer drift, makes point-in-time two-cut and replay-contract-sensitive, narrows sealed packaging to non-authoritative copying absent migration proof, and defines a disposability negative control.
keyFindings: Authority is selected per mode by authority state and epoch; a verified typed-ledger graph remains shadow-only before governed cutover
Domain and authorization-audit ledgers are complementary evidence streams, not competing authorities, and denial or unapplied-allow evidence never becomes domain state
Checkpoint validity binds immutable reducer implementation and replay-contract digests, so same-version code or configuration drift invalidates reuse
Point-in-time queries require an explicit domain cut, audit cut, and replay contract rather than an invented cross-ledger order
Sealed packaging is only a copy until governed storage migration and retained-reader parity authorize replacement; committed ledger deletion remains forbidden
Projection disposability is proven by isolated deletion and byte-identical rebuild without changing authority or accepted behavior

ruledOut.approach: Choose authority by the freshest graph or checkpoint
ruledOut.reason: Authority is a per-mode state-and-epoch CAS decision, not a freshness property

ruledOut.approach: Create one synthetic sequence across domain and audit ledgers
ruledOut.reason: Separate sequence domains support only explicit authorization links and declared cut watermarks

ruledOut.approach: Treat a reducer version label as complete implementation identity
ruledOut.reason: An unchanged label cannot detect reducer-code, canonicalization, registry, schema, or configuration drift

ruledOut.approach: Delete committed frames after export or sealed packaging
ruledOut.reason: A copy does not prove governed storage replacement, byte recovery, audit linkage, or retained archival-reader parity

nextFocus: P3 golden parity harness event-shape and negative-control audit
